# Tokens

> Every token name the published CSS gives you, what each one is for, and its value.

Part of the [Nate Mills Design System](../README.md). These 86 names are the core tokens [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md) lists for building pages: write `var(--name)`, never the raw value. tokens.css declares more (motion, weights, stacking, component tokens); every one is in [tokens.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/n8mills-UI/nate-mills-design-system/main/tokens.json) with its description. Each purpose below comes from that description, each value from [DESIGN.md](../DESIGN.md) or tokens.json, and the last column is the token's path in tokens.json, its DTCG source. All foundations: [Foundations](README.md).

## Three tiers

Every token in tokens.json sits in one of three tiers. Build with semantic tokens.

| Tier | What it is | Example | Where it is listed | Use it? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Primitive | A raw value, named by hue and stop. | `--neutral-850` (`#1c1c1f`) | Only in tokens.json, in the neutral, lime, yellow, alpha groups. | Never pick one: primitives are the source semantic tokens read from. |
| Semantic | A role: what the value is for, such as reading text or the gap between sections. | `--color-text-primary` (`#0a0a0b`; dark `#f4f4f5`, from `--neutral-950`) | This page lists the 86 core ones; the rest are in tokens.json. | Yes: pick these for anything you build. |
| Component | One component's own value, usually aliasing a semantic token. | `--card-bg` (`#ffffff`; dark `#1c1c1f`, from `--color-surface`) | The Tokens table on each [component page](../COMPONENTS.md). | Only to restyle that one component; never reuse one elsewhere. |

One way, top to bottom: a component token aliases a semantic token, a semantic token aliases a primitive, and a primitive is a literal. Nothing reaches back up. The primary button is the one deliberate shortcut: its fill aliases the brand lime directly, so it keeps the brand in every theme.

## Colour

The same names in every theme; the dark column shows the value the dark theme gives each one. Brand and on-ink colours are fixed, so both columns match.

| Token | Use it for | Value | Dark value | Source in tokens.json |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--brand-primary` | The brand lime, scarce on purpose: the primary button fill, brand outlines, focus rings on dark surfaces and status dots. Never body text on a light surface. | `#d2ff37` | `#d2ff37` | `brand.primary` |
| `--brand-primary-dim` | Hover-dim step of the brand lime (lime.600). | `#b8e030` | `#b8e030` | `brand.primary-dim` |
| `--brand-primary-vivid` | The hot vivid-yellow end of brand.gradient: yellow.500, the house secondary. Gradient stop only. | `#eeff00` | `#eeff00` | `brand.primary-vivid` |
| `--brand-secondary` | The second brand colour, lime's partner: the yellow the brand gradient runs into. The Theme lab repaints it per preset from the preset's heading colour (Rave keeps its authored hot pink), so a theme's Secondary set is the second colour you actually see on its page. | `#eeff00` | `#eeff00` | `brand.secondary` |
| `--brand-ink` | Fixed, theme-invariant brand ink. The always-dark bed, and the dark foreground on a fixed lime or static-white bed. | `#1c1c1f` | `#1c1c1f` | `brand.ink` |
| `--brand-gradient` | CSS-only composite; reads var(--brand-primary) and var(--brand-spot) so the gradient follows a brand re-point at CSS level. The explicit 'in oklab' preserves the perceptual midpoint the gradient had when its stops were oklch(): rgb()/hex stops interpolate in sRGB by default, which would shift the blend by up to 11/255. | `linear-gradient(135deg in oklab, #d2ff37 0%, #eeff00 100%)` | `linear-gradient(135deg in oklab, #d2ff37 0%, #eeff00 100%)` | `brand.gradient` |
| `--color-bg` | The page canvas. Brand off-white in light, near-black in dark. | `#f5f5f5` | `#0a0a0b` | `color.bg` |
| `--color-surface` | The default card / panel surface. White card on the grey page in light (a genuine lift); the lighter near-black (#1c1c1f) in dark. | `#ffffff` | `#1c1c1f` | `color.surface` |
| `--color-surface-sunken` | Recessed wells, insets, thumbnails, chips. A step below the card surface: light grey in light; the darker near-black (#141416) in dark. | `#ececec` | `#141416` | `color.surface-sunken` |
| `--color-surface-inverse` | A slab that stays near-black in both themes, like the testimonials band. | `#0a0a0b` | `#0a0a0b` | `color.surface-inverse` |
| `--color-text-primary` | Default reading text. Near-black on light, near-white on dark. | `#0a0a0b` | `#f4f4f5` | `color.text-primary` |
| `--color-text-secondary` | Secondary text: supporting copy one step quieter than text-primary. | `#3f3f46` | `#a1a1aa` | `color.text-secondary` |
| `--color-text-tertiary` | Tertiary text: section labels and quiet meta copy; the last step that still clears 4.5:1 on light. | `#67676f` | `#909096` | `color.text-tertiary` |
| `--color-border` | Default hairline border and divider colour, theme-aware. | `#e4e4e7` | `#27272a` | `color.border` |
| `--color-border-strong` | Heavier border for edges that must read past a hairline (secondary-button outlines). | `#d4d4d8` | `#3f3f46` | `color.border-strong` |
| `--color-border-brand` | The brand-lime outline accent (active selection, link underline, brand ring). Theme-invariant lime, never overridden per theme; the semantic the brand outlines read instead of the raw primitive. | `#d2ff37` | `#d2ff37` | `color.border-brand` |
| `--color-accent` | The single theme-aware interactive role: ink on light, brand lime on dark. Active and selected states. | `#1c1c1f` | `#d2ff37` | `color.accent` |
| `--color-accent-hover` | Hover step of the accent role. | `#0a0a0b` | `#b8e030` | `color.accent-hover` |
| `--color-on-accent` | Text or icons sitting on an accent fill; the contrast pair of color.accent. | `#ffffff` | `#0a0a0b` | `color.on-accent` |
| `--color-focus-ring` | Theme-aware keyboard-focus colour: ink on light, lime on dark. Consumed via border.focus. | `#1c1c1f` | `#d2ff37` | `color.focus-ring` |
| `--color-link` | Underlined navigational link text: ink on light, lime on dark. Distinct role from accent (Section 10). | `#1c1c1f` | `#d2ff37` | `color.link` |
| `--color-link-hover` | Link hover colour. | `#0a0a0b` | `#ffffff` | `color.link-hover` |
| `--color-on-ink-primary` | Primary text on an always-dark slab (88% white). | `rgb(255 255 255 / 0.88)` | `rgb(255 255 255 / 0.88)` | `color.on-ink-primary` |
| `--color-on-ink-secondary` | Secondary text on an always-dark slab (66% white). | `rgb(255 255 255 / 0.66)` | `rgb(255 255 255 / 0.66)` | `color.on-ink-secondary` |
| `--color-on-ink-muted` | Quiet fills and inactive dots on an always-dark slab. Not a text colour. | `rgb(255 255 255 / 0.4)` | `rgb(255 255 255 / 0.4)` | `color.on-ink-muted` |
| `--color-on-ink-border` | Hairline border on an always-dark slab (8% white). | `rgb(255 255 255 / 0.08)` | `rgb(255 255 255 / 0.08)` | `color.on-ink-border` |
| `--color-feedback-background-error` | Error message backgrounds: deep red on light, soft red on dark. | `#961010` | `#ff8f8f` | `color.feedback-background-error` |
| `--color-on-feedback-error` | Contrast pair for content sitting on feedback-background-error: white on the deep light-theme red, near-black red on the soft dark-theme red. 8.7:1 light, 8.9:1 dark. | `#ffffff` | `#2a0000` | `color.on-feedback-error` |
| `--color-overlay-soft` | Soft scrim behind floating chrome (35% black). | `rgb(0 0 0 / 0.35)` | `rgb(0 0 0 / 0.35)` | `color.overlay-soft` |
| `--color-overlay-base` | Standard modal and lightbox scrim (62% black). | `rgb(0 0 0 / 0.62)` | `rgb(0 0 0 / 0.62)` | `color.overlay-base` |
| `--color-overlay-strong` | Heavy scrim for maximum content isolation (88% black). | `rgb(0 0 0 / 0.88)` | `rgb(0 0 0 / 0.88)` | `color.overlay-strong` |

## Font families

| Token | Use it for | Value | Source in tokens.json |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--font-display` | Display headings and large numbers. Anton, one weight, never faux-bolded. | `"Anton", Impact, "Haettenschweiler", sans-serif` | `font.display` |
| `--font-body` | Body copy, lists, and buttons. | `"Work Sans", "Work Sans Fallback", -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", sans-serif` | `font.body` |
| `--font-mono` | Tabular numbers, code, and eyebrow labels. | `"JetBrains Mono", ui-monospace, "SF Mono", Menlo, Consolas, monospace` | `font.mono` |

## Type styles

Size, weight, line height and tracking for the named styles on the Typography page.

| Token | Use it for | Value | Source in tokens.json |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--display-hero` | Display type at hero scale, fluid 40 to 118px. This site’s own hero headline is a documented exception: it sets its own clamps and runs larger still. | `clamp(2.5rem, 9vw, 7.375rem)` | `display.hero` |
| `--display-weight` | The single weight every display preset carries: regular (400), the one weight Anton ships. Asking for more would send Figma looking for an Anton SemiBold that does not exist. | `400` | `display.weight` |
| `--line-display` | Display-grade headings (--text-h1, section h2s). Big text wants the tightest leading. | `1.05` | `line.display` |
| `--display-tight` | Display tracking. Pairs with every heading above card size, the hero included. | `-0.0176em` | `display.tight` |
| `--display-section` | Section headings (every section h2). .section-title consumes this; the About headings are a documented exception in sections.css (Hi, I'm Nate opens the section and fills its column; the headline over the story fills its column and stays under 85% of it). | `clamp(min(4.25rem, 19vw), 8.7vw, 7.5rem)` | `display.section` |
| `--weight-extrabold` | Five distinct weights. The body face loads 400 to 800 as one variable file; the display face ships a single 400, so font-synthesis is off site-wide. | `800` | `weight.extrabold` |
| `--text-h1` | The base display size every other heading size is derived from. | `clamp(2.125rem, 5.8vw, 4.5rem)` | `text.h1` |
| `--text-h2` | Card titles, intro lines, sub-headings inside section bodies. | `clamp(1.375rem, 4vw, 2rem)` | `text.h2` |
| `--line-heading` | Card titles and section sub-headings (--text-h2, UTH section heads). | `1.15` | `line.heading` |
| `--tracking-tight` | -0.02em. Tightens large text below display size. | `-0.02em` | `tracking.tight` |
| `--display-card-title` | Large feature-card and tile titles. | `clamp(1.375rem, 4vw, 2.75rem)` | `display.card-title` |
| `--display-stat-num` | Oversized numerals for a stat callout (tabular, e.g. 1,248). | `clamp(2.5rem, 7vw, 5.5rem)` | `display.stat-num` |
| `--display-intro` | Section intro lines and emphasis copy under a heading. | `clamp(1.25rem, 5vw, 1.5rem)` | `display.intro` |
| `--weight-regular` | 400. Body copy and captions. | `400` | `weight.regular` |
| `--line-snug` | Intro lines, award titles, compact meta text. A half-step tighter than body. | `1.45` | `line.snug` |
| `--text-body` | Paragraphs, lists, default reading text, card body copy. | `1rem` | `text.body` |
| `--line-body` | Default reading text: paragraphs, lists, captions. The workhorse. | `1.5` | `line.body` |
| `--tracking-normal` | 0. The body default; most text sits here. | `0` | `tracking.normal` |
| `--size-sm` | 14px. Compact body: footer text, card bullets, dense UI copy. | `0.875rem` | `size.sm` |
| `--text-caption` | Tiny captions, footnotes, stat descriptions. | `0.75rem` | `text.caption` |
| `--text-label` | Uppercase mono labels, eyebrows, stat labels, badges. | `0.6875rem` | `text.label` |
| `--weight-medium` | 500. UI text, chips, mono labels. | `500` | `weight.medium` |
| `--tracking-label` | Small uppercase labels. | `0.08em` | `tracking.label` |

## Radius

| Token | Use it for | Value | Source in tokens.json |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--radius-none` | Square. No rounding, for sharp-cornered surfaces and full-bleed media. | `0` | `radius.none` |
| `--radius-sm` | Small radius. The workhorse for inputs and small controls; chips, badges and buttons take the full radius. | `8px` | `radius.sm` |
| `--radius-md` | Medium radius. Mid-size controls and insets, a touch rounder than sm. | `10px` | `radius.md` |
| `--radius-lg` | Large radius. The social links (--sbtn-radius) and other mid-weight containers. | `14px` | `radius.lg` |
| `--radius-xl` | Extra-large radius. The default for cards and modals (--card-radius), prominent panels and feature surfaces. | `20px` | `radius.xl` |
| `--radius-full` | Full round. Pills, tags, and circular buttons; forces a complete radius at any height. | `999px` | `radius.full` |

## Spacing

| Token | Use it for | Value | Source in tokens.json |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--space-50` | Half step under the base. Optical nudges: an alias line under its token, a count chip's inset, the burger bars. | `2px` | `space.50` |
| `--space-100` | Hairline gap. Icon-to-label, tight inline spacing. | `4px` | `space.100` |
| `--space-200` | Tight gap. Chip padding, small stacks. | `8px` | `space.200` |
| `--space-250` | Dense-row gap between tight and medium-tight. The drawer's dense rows, the footer closer, the feature badges. | `10px` | `space.250` |
| `--space-300` | Medium-tight break. Heading-to-body, compact rows. | `12px` | `space.300` |
| `--space-400` | Base unit. Default gap between related elements; the compact card-padding tier (--card-pad-compact). | `16px` | `space.400` |
| `--space-500` | Medium break. Group separation inside a section; the standard card-padding tier (--card-pad-standard). | `24px` | `space.500` |
| `--space-600` | Large gap. Between subsections and card to card; the spacious card-padding tier (--card-pad-spacious). | `32px` | `space.600` |
| `--space-700` | Block spacing between stacked content blocks. | `48px` | `space.700` |
| `--space-800` | Major block separation and section inner padding. | `64px` | `space.800` |
| `--space-900` | Section rhythm. The lower bound of vertical section padding (--section-padding). | `96px` | `space.900` |
| `--space-1000` | Very large block space. The design-system doc's closing space and the orbit specimen's size. | `128px` | `space.1000` |
| `--space-1100` | Outsized spacing for full-bleed editorial breaks. | `192px` | `space.1100` |
| `--space-1200` | Largest step. The upper bound of vertical section padding (--section-padding), reached only on very large screens; otherwise rare, marquee-scale vertical space. | `256px` | `space.1200` |
| `--section-padding` | The vertical padding of every page section, fluid between its lower and upper bounds. | `clamp(96px, min(14.2vh, 12vw), 256px)` | `section-padding` |
| `--card-pad-compact` | Compact card-padding tier (16px). Dense content tiles: credential cards, health-check tiles, inner controls. | `16px` | `card-pad.compact` |
| `--card-pad-standard` | Standard card-padding tier (24px). The default content-card inset; matches the base .card. | `24px` | `card-pad.standard` |
| `--card-pad-spacious` | Spacious card-padding tier (32px). Large feature, award, and full-testimonial cards (often the desktop step up from standard). | `32px` | `card-pad.spacious` |

## Borders, focus and targets

| Token | Use it for | Value | Source in tokens.json |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--border-hairline` | Default 1px hairline border; reads --color-border so it follows the theme. The standard card edge and divider. | `1px solid var(--color-border)` | `border.hairline` |
| `--border-strong` | Heavier 1px border; reads --color-border-strong. For edges that need to read past a hairline, such as interactive-card hover outlines. | `1px solid var(--color-border-strong)` | `border.strong` |
| `--border-focus` | 2px focus outline; reads --color-focus-ring (ink on light, lime on dark). The keyboard-focus indicator, never removed without a replacement. | `2px solid var(--color-focus-ring)` | `border.focus` |
| `--focus-ring-offset` | Offset between an element and its focus ring. Outsets the 2px ring so it clears the element edge. | `2px` | `focus-ring-offset` |
| `--touch-target-min` | The smallest pointer target for any control a finger or pointer taps. | `44px` | `touch-target-min` |
